name: CKA Cluster Operations
description: Node-level cluster administration you can't practice in CK-X: static pods, repairing a broken control-plane component, CSR approval, node draining, and etcd backup.
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture + Troubleshooting. Prove you can operate the cluster node-side: static pods, control-plane repair, CSR approval, cordon/drain, and etcd backup.

questions.title: Static pod on a worker
questions.prompt:
On the worker node `$W1` (run `kindlab up` to see node names — e.g. `kindlab-worker`), create a **static pod** named `static-web` using image `nginx:alpine` by placing a manifest in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` on that node.

The kubelet will create a mirror pod named `static-web-<node>` in the `default` namespace. Verify it is Running.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it <node> bash`, then write the manifest; the pod name in the manifest should be `static-web`.

verification.description: Static pod manifest present on the worker node

questions.title: Repair a broken control-plane component
questions.prompt:
The **kube-scheduler** is down — someone added a bad flag to its static pod manifest on the control-plane node, so it crash-loops and new pods won't schedule.

Find and fix it (the manifest is `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` on `$CP`) so the scheduler becomes healthy again.

_Hint:_ `docker exec -it $CP bash`, inspect the manifest, remove the bogus flag; the kubelet restarts the static pod automatically.

verification.description: kube-scheduler static pod is Ready again

questions.title: Approve a CertificateSigningRequest
questions.prompt:
A CertificateSigningRequest named `developer` is **Pending** (a new user needs a client cert). Approve it.

_Hint:_ `kubectl get csr`, then `kubectl certificate approve developer`.

questions.title: Cordon and drain a node
questions.prompt:
Node `$W2` needs maintenance. **Cordon** it so no new pods schedule there, then **drain** it (evict existing workloads, ignoring DaemonSets).

_Hint:_ `kubectl cordon $W2` then `kubectl drain $W2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`.

questions.title: Back up etcd
questions.prompt:
Take an **etcd snapshot** and save it to `/opt/snapshot.db` on the control-plane node `$CP`.

_Hint:_ run `etcdctl snapshot save` from inside the etcd pod (it has etcdctl + the certs), saving to a path under `/var/lib/etcd` (which is mounted on the node), then copy it to `/opt/snapshot.db`. See answers for the exact commands.

verification.description: Snapshot file exists at /opt/snapshot.db on the control-plane
Snapshot is a real (non-trivial) etcd backup
